csv_project_name: AE for Packwood (55S) & S Lewis County Toledo Airports
csv_scope_of_work: Lewis County Department of Public Works is soliciting Statements of Qualifications (SOQs) from qualified consulting firms with expertise who wish to be evaluated and considered to provide Airport Engineering Services for the Packwood (55S) and South Lewis County Ed Carlson Memorial Toledo (TDO) Airports in Lewis County, Washington. Lewis County owns and operates two general aviation airports. The South Lewis County Ed Carlson Memorial (TDO) airport and the Packwood (55S) airports. The South Lewis County Ed Carlson Memorial (TDO airport is a local general aviation (GA) airport located three miles northeast of the City of Toledo, WA. It has a runway length of 4,479 feet and width of 150 feet with a based aircraft fleet of 39 single engine airplanes and 2 helicopters. The Packwood Airport (55S) is a basic general aviation (GA) airport located approximately mile southwest of the Packwood Town Center in unincorporated Lewis County. The airport has a runway length of 2,356 feet and width of 60 feet with a based aircraft fleet of 1 and with 5,300 operations annually. This work is to provide Professional Engineer Services to support future architectural, engineering, environmental, design, plans, specifications, engineer s estimates of probable construction costs, construction/inspection, and other related professional services for projects identified on each of the 5-year Capital Improvement Plans for both airports.

short_description: Consulting services for airport engineering and capital improvement projects at two general aviation airports.
project_location: Toledo and Packwood, Lewis County, Washington, USA
project_scope: Provision of professional engineering support for two Lewis County general aviation airports under their 5-year Capital Improvement Plans. South Lewis County Ed Carlson Memorial Toledo Airport (TDO) is located three miles northeast of Toledo, WA and has a runway 4,479 ft long and 150 ft wide, with 39 single-engine aircraft and 2 helicopters based there. Packwood Airport (55S) is located about one mile southwest of Packwood Town Center and has a runway 2,356 ft long and 60 ft wide, with 1 based aircraft and about 5,300 annual operations. Scope includes support for future architectural, engineering, environmental, design, plans, specifications, engineer's estimates of probable construction costs, construction/inspection, and related professional services.
services: Airport engineering services; professional engineering; architectural and engineering support; environmental services; design; preparation of plans and specifications; cost estimating; construction inspection; related professional services.
relevance_explanation:
- Airport engineering framework-type consulting opportunity, not a clearly defined bridge, building, roof, or special structure project.
- Scope is broad and multidisciplinary with no specific structurally demanding component identified.
- Primarily transportation/aviation infrastructure planning and engineering rather than sbp core focus areas.
- Could include some building or structural tasks in future CIP projects, but this is not specified.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction budget is stated. The notice references future projects under 5-year Capital Improvement Plans for two airports, but provides no cost figures or defined project list, so a realistic total construction cost estimate is not possible from the available information.
fee_explanation: No fee information is provided. The solicitation is for on-call/professional airport engineering services tied to future CIP projects, without a stated contract value or construction budget.
references_qualifications: Qualified consulting firms with expertise in airport engineering services are invited to submit Statements of Qualifications. No specific minimum number or type of reference projects is stated in the provided text.
